newsitem.title: CHINA: China's B share indices mixed in dull trading.
newsitem.headline: China's B share indices mixed in dull trading.

text.p: China's B share indices closed mixed in dull trading on Thursday, the first session of 1997, with the holiday doldrums still prevailing, brokers said.
The Shanghai B share index fell 1.91 percent to 65.743 points on turnover of US$5.3 million, down from $7.7 million in the previous session.
Brokers said the index slipped on profit-taking in property developer Shanghai Lujiazui Finance.
"Most investors are not yet back from holidays, which made the trading sluggish," one Shanghai broker said.
The Shenzhen B index rose 1.45 percent to 147.59 on turnover of HK$168 million against Tuesday's HK$279 million.
"Institutions were largely sidelined (on Thursday) due to a lack of major market-moving news," a Shenzhen broker said.
Investors were seen building positions in issues expected to release strong 1996 results, brokers in both markets said.
"Most listed firms will see their results improved because of the two cuts in China's bank interest rates in 1996," one analyst said.
In Shanghai, construction machinery maker Jintai was the biggest loser on expectations of poor results, falling 8.25 percent to US$0.200.
In Shenzhen, Guangdong Power rose 5.41 percent to HK$7.21 after 2.28 million shares changed hands on investor optimism over the power supplier's 1996 results, brokers said.

Domestic A share indices in both Shanghai and Shenzhen rallied on Thursday after losses in the previous session, but trading was dull with a wait-and-see mood dominating the market in the aftermath of the New Year holiday, brokers said.
Shanghai's A index inched up 0.34 percent to 958.190 points on turnover of 2.3 billion yuan, falling from 3.9 billion yuan in the last session of 1996.
Shenzhen A shares rallied 2.11 percent to end at 349.02, on turnover of 5.80 billion yuan, compared with 7.15 billion yuan on Tuesday.
